structured_output.summary:
Since about E084, every positive accuracy effect in this loop is ≤0.12 pp and comes from one process or one distinct scored sample. The real effects are all negative: E092 −0.18, E093 −0.44, E078/E079 −0.18, E083 −0.29 and E082's collapse. Losses are easy to find and gains are not, which looks like a local optimum. The tree keeps building mechanisms (H10.2, H11, H8.2) on deltas the size of the noise.

There are three problems. First, the noise model probably tells the loop to do the wrong thing. Under the deterministic SGD recipe, where process noise was zero, neutral changes already moved the 3-seed mean by 0.2–0.3 pp (E004, E011). That means any recipe change re-draws every seed's trajectory. Adding processes doesn't shrink that part of the noise; only more seeds do, and untimed seeds cost about 4.5 s each. E106's process sd of 0.03 pp also doesn't fit the 0.2 pp scored sd from E101.

Second, the pooled off-seed data contradict the current story. E100's off-seed mean is 0.7527, against 0.7525 for E090. So the 32 px Muon ×1.25 plus the window pin are worth about +0.01 pp in total. E100's whole advantage over E090 sits in seeds 0–2, and "robustly banked" is unsupported. H10.2 should be refuted, not left open. E111's claim to support H11 builds on that null effect. E108's +0.09 off-seed, the best multi-process signal the loop has, points against H11. It was also judged more harshly than E110, a scored high draw that the off-seed runs didn't back.

Third, the bookkeeping has drifted. The H2, H4 and H7 statements are out of date. Verdicts in predictions.tsv contradict the tree's statuses (E104 versus H10.1.1, E102 to E105). The free log analyses (kernel-name clustering, within-seed sd) have been requested at least five times and never done.

Directions never tried: tuning the lookahead and final-EMA strength under Muon (the one demonstrated, untuned, structural accuracy source), untimed profiling for depth cuts and group-3 width, and the H12 data-composition levers. None of these zero-time levers can be judged without a 100+-seed paired instrument. Finally, the loop should decide whether its gate instrument is seeds 0–2 or the population. Its current mix of scored keeps and off-seed closes selects for luck.

critiques.target: H4 (noise model and the '>=3 fresh processes per arm' rule)
critiques.issue: The rule assumes per-process cuDNN divergence is the main source of noise. E106 measured process sd of the 22-seed off-seed mean at only ~0.03 pp. Under the deterministic SGD recipe, where process noise was zero, neutral perturbations still moved the 3-seed mean by 0.2–0.3 pp (E004 post-mortem, E011). That points to a third component: any recipe change chaotically re-draws every seed's trajectory, with per-seed sd ~0.3–0.4 pp. More processes do not reduce this. Only more seeds do. With 22 seeds the SE of a recipe-vs-recipe difference is ~0.09–0.1 pp however many processes run. So E107/E108/E110/E111 (±0.03–0.09 pp with 2–3 processes) are all ≤1 SE, and so is the 'refuted at ±0.04' wording in E111.
critiques.suggestion: Swap processes for seeds. Untimed trials cost ~4.5 s, so 100–150 seeds per arm in one process takes ~10 min and gives a paired-difference SE of ~0.04 pp. First calibrate the null: run a math-neutral perturbation of E100 on the same 100 seeds (e.g. reordered param groups or a different but equivalent fusion), as the retired H4.2.1 proposed. Report the observed sd of the difference, and set the support/refute thresholds at about 2x that.

critiques.issue: The scored instrument shows a 3-seed mean sd of ~0.2 pp across identical-code processes (E101: 0.7561 vs 0.7516), which implies a per-seed cross-process sd of ~0.35 pp. The off-seed side script shows a 22-seed mean process sd of ~0.03 pp (E106), which implies a per-seed sd of ~0.14 pp. E098 then showed a 0.25 pp gap on 8 seeds. These figures cannot all come from the same iid noise. Either process noise comes in clusters (H4.4/H4.5 pick sets), or the side script differs from the scored harness in something that changes cuDNN or Inductor picks (shared autotune cache, memory state, process launch path).
critiques.suggestion: Run seeds 0–2 through the side script in 3+ fresh processes and compare with the three distinct scored E100 samples. Finish the H4.5 kernel-name clustering and the H4.2.8 within-seed sd calculation from logs that already exist (E094, E098, E106 per-seed vectors and checksums). Do this before any further A/B. Every threshold in the tree currently rests on a noise figure that has been guessed rather than measured.

critiques.target: E106 verdict 'E100 robustly banked' and H10.2.1
critiques.issue: Pooled off-seed E100 is 0.7527 (3 processes, seeds 3–24). E090 is 0.7525 (E098) and ~0.7526 (E094 distinct mean). So E100 − E090 ≈ +0.01 pp. The 32 px ×1.25 factor plus the window pin together show no population effect. E100's lead over E090 (scored 0.7543 vs 0.7515) exists only on seeds 0–2. That is either a recipe×seed interaction or luck, and the off-seed instrument cannot see it. H10.2.1 should not read 'weakly supports'.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H10.2.1 refuted, or at best null, at the population level. Rewrite the H2/H4 tip description: E100 is feasible on seeds 0–2 in 3/3 distinct samples, but its population mean is ~0.7527, the same as E090. Treat E100's margin as a property of the fixed scored seeds, and settle whether that property persists (see the gate-instrument critique).

critiques.issue: It is still 'open' at 0.20 even though both phase-local tests failed (E107 low-res: −0.02; E111 28 px: +0.03). The one remaining support, 32 px ×1.25, is null against E090 when pooled. The dose-response is not monotone either (E110 at ×1.5: −0.07 vs ×1.25). Nothing in the results supports the mechanism.
critiques.suggestion: Refute H10.2 and fold the conclusion into H7.1: Muon lr is flat at 0.20–0.36 across every phase and base tested (E034, E105, E107, E110, E111). Close Muon lr scaling as a lever and stop spending runs on it.

critiques.issue: E111 concludes 'the factor helps only in the 32 px phase, consistent with H11'. That builds on the 32 px factor having an effect, and the pooled data show it has none. The one multi-process test that discriminates H11 from H8, E108 (moving 0.25 ep from 32 px into 0.5 ep at 24 px), gave +0.09 off-seed over 3 processes. H11 predicts a negative result. E090's 28 px substitution 'cost' (−0.25 pp) was measured against scored pools and one off-seed process.
critiques.suggestion: Lower H11 to ≤0.15 and remove E111 as support. If the large-seed instrument is built, rerun E108 against E100 on 100+ seeds. That single A/B decides H8.2 versus H11.

critiques.issue: E108 and E109 both scored 0.7527 and are probably bit-identical, so they count as one distinct scored sample under the loop's own H4 rule. Yet the scored −0.16 pp was set against the 3-process off-seed +0.09 and the result called 'conflicting/inconclusive'. In E110 the loop correctly let multi-process off-seed override a high single scored draw. Applying the same rule here makes E108 the strongest positive multi-process signal in the recent loop, at only +0.3% time.
critiques.suggestion: Apply the instruments the same way in both directions. Record E108 as leaning toward support for H8.2. Explore one more step in that direction (e.g. 2@16 + 2.0@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.25@32) on a high-seed-count instrument, and check whether the gain funds a ~1.5% 32 px trim.

critiques.target: H2 (Lvl1 statement: 'schedule and batch reshuffles have converged')
critiques.issue: The '0.04–0.065 pp per 1%' exchange rates come from single-process deltas of ~0.1 pp over 2.5–5% time changes, so each rate has an SE about as large as the rate. Calling the trades 'equal everywhere', and therefore converged, cannot be distinguished from 'the accuracy surface is flat within ±0.1 pp and we can't resolve it'. The statement is also stale: it still lists E100 at n=2 (0.7561/0.7516) after E106 added 0.7551.
critiques.suggestion: Restate H2's conclusion as 'unresolved at the current instrument resolution' rather than 'converged'. Update the tip numbers, attach an SE to every rate, and recompute the rates once a large-seed instrument exists.

critiques.target: Gate instrument (applies to H4, H2, keep/discard policy)
critiques.issue: Off-seed means estimate the population mean, which matters for the official 40-seed 0.75 bar. That bar is already cleared by ~0.25–0.3 pp. The binding constraint is the local gate on fixed seeds 0–2. The tree holds two incompatible positions. If recipe changes re-draw seeds chaotically (H4: 'pairing barely reduces variance'), seeds 0–2 carry no persistent recipe-specific offset, and E100, with a population mean of ~0.7527, would pass only about half the time. Its 3/3 passes would then be luck. If instead a persistent recipe×seed component exists, off-seed is the wrong instrument for the gate, and many closes made on off-seed evidence were made on the wrong quantity.
critiques.suggestion: Settle this directly. Take a cheap time cut (e.g. E088's trim) and E100, run seeds 0–2 in 5+ processes each, and compare the spread of the 0–2 mean with the off-seed difference. State in H4 which instrument decides keeps and which decides closes, and use it consistently.

critiques.issue: Several verdicts contradict the tree. E104 is logged as 'refutes H10.1.1', but H10.1.1 says it 'leans toward support'. E105 'refutes H7.1.3', E103 'refutes H6.5.4' and E102 'refutes H11.1.1', but all three nodes are marked inconclusive. E107/E111 'refute H10.2', which remains open. H7 still says Muon lr on the mixed-batch tip is 'untested' after E105/E107/E110/E111. E104's own post-mortem calls it 'placement-independent (refutes early steps worth more)', but the H8 statement still claims early phases are the highest-value ones.
critiques.suggestion: Reconcile the two files in one pass. Each verdict token should match the node status. Update the H7, H8 and H10 text with E104–E111.

critiques.target: H4.5 / H4.2.8 / H4.2.4 (free analyses never done)
critiques.issue: Kernel-name logs were requested in E067, E081, E094, E098, E099 and E106 and have never been analyzed. The within-seed cross-process sd, the 'free first step' of H4.2.8, has not been computed. The provenance mismatches in H4.2.4 (E092/E093/E103/E105 bases) are unresolved. These analyses cost nothing and determine whether past off-seed verdicts hold at all.
critiques.suggestion: Before any new scored run, do the log-only analyses. Cluster processes by pick set against their run means, compute the per-seed cross-process sd from E106's 3×22 vectors, and git-diff the ambiguous bases. Retire H4.5 or promote it depending on the result.

critiques.target: Untried direction: lookahead-EMA and final-EMA strength under Muon (H6/H6.8)
critiques.issue: E092 shows the SGD-era lookahead carries ~0.2–0.3 pp under Muon, and E079 shows the final EMA carries ~0.18 pp. These are the largest structural accuracy sources still in the recipe, and their parameters (lookahead cadence and alpha, final-EMA lerp 0.3) were inherited from SGD or Fable and never tuned under Muon. Only the EMA window length was varied (E081/E083). H6 was retired before these knobs were swept.
critiques.suggestion: Run a small zero-time sweep of lookahead alpha and cadence (e.g. every 2/3/5 steps, alpha ±30%) and of final-EMA lerp (0.2/0.4), judged on the large-seed instrument. This is the one 'scalar' family with a demonstrated effect size of ≥0.2 pp.

critiques.issue: These are the only time levers left that don't spend accuracy margin, and both are still queued behind accuracy A/Bs. The H2.19 premise that 576 channels already pay for 640 on 128-wide tiles is shaky. Under pure 128-wide quantization, E080's 352 should have recovered ~0% of its FLOP saving, but it recovered 33%. Wgrad and elementwise work also scale linearly. So 640 is unlikely to be 'near-free'.
critiques.suggestion: Run both untimed profiles now; they cost no margin. For H2.19, read the group-3 kernel tile shapes first, as the node already specifies. For H2.18, require the ≥6% projected saving before any scored run, and expect the capacity loss to look like E017 (−0.94 pp for −8%).

critiques.issue: H12 has never been tested, and its predicted effects (≥+0.1 pp) sit at or below the current instrument's resolution. H12.1 (2 augmented copies at 32 px) halves unique-image coverage in the phase the loop believes binds, at only ~7 epochs. Under SGD, extra augmentation hurt (E008). Its downside risk is larger than the node's framing suggests.
critiques.suggestion: Prioritize H12.2 (stratified batches; essentially no downside) and H12.3 (translate 4 in the late phases) over H12.1. Run them only on the large-seed paired instrument. If H12.1 is run, use 1.5 copies (e.g. 768 unique + 256 repeats) rather than 2x.

critiques.issue: H9 was retired at 0.10, yet everything since has borne out its core prediction that scalar knobs are null. Muon lr in four forms (E105, E107, E110, E111), the whitening-bias window (E102) and BN-stat averaging (E103) all came back null. The only non-null changes were structural removals (E092, E093). The retirement is not supported by the results.
critiques.suggestion: Either restore H9 as the operating policy (stop generating scalar variants, rank candidates by expected structural effect ≥0.15 pp), or record the evidence that refuted it. Drop H2.11.5 (bs 768) on the same grounds: E104 already prices added steps at ~0.04 pp per 1%, and wave quantization makes bs 768 worse.
